title: An Insect Declared Extinct Was Found Alive on One Bush, 80 Years Later
subject: Lord Howe Island stick insect

scenes.text: An extinct insect was hiding under one bush.
The Lord Howe Island stick insect, fifteen centimetres long, nicknamed the tree lobster. In 1918 a ship ran aground there, and rats came ashore.
Within a couple of years the rats had eaten every one anyone could find. By the nineteen thirties it was gone. Extinct.
Ball's Pyramid: a bare sea stack 562 metres tall, twenty kilometres away. In 2001, climbers checked one shrub on a ledge, at night.
Under it, 24 insects. The entire species, on one plant.
Two pairs went to Melbourne Zoo. Thousands have hatched since. Extinct for eighty years, saved by one bush.

description:
The Lord Howe Island stick insect, a 15-centimetre 'tree lobster', was wiped out by rats that came ashore from a shipwreck in 1918 and was declared extinct.
In 2001 climbers found 24 of them living under a single shrub on a ledge of Ball's Pyramid, a 562-metre sea stack about 20 kilometres away. Two pairs were taken to Melbourne Zoo in 2003 and the breeding programme has since produced thousands.
Which extinct animal would you most want found alive?
first_comment: Ball's Pyramid is the tallest volcanic sea stack on Earth, and almost nothing grows on it. Which extinct animal would you most want to see rediscovered?
